source.title: Tame distillation and desingularization by p-alterations
source.version: The published Annals article (30 pages, pp. 97–126), freely available from the journal, read completely; locators are its page numbers. arXiv:1508.06255v2 ('final version', 24 pages, SHA-256 24f67ac3…) was compared and has the same statements and numbering.
readSections: 2026-09-29: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 97–126, all pages: §§1–4 and references; page images checked at every source issue.

2026-09-30, Codex codex-rtOQ9t: fix-specific reread of published pp. 104, 113, 115, 117–119 and 121–124, with images at pp. 117 and 123; Exposé X §§3.3.3–3.5 and Temkin 2010 Theorems 1.1/1.5, Corollary 1.6 checked separately. The earlier complete reading is preserved as provenance.

summary: Temkin strengthens Gabber's ℓ′-alteration theorem so that the resolving alteration has degree divisible only by residue characteristics. Any scheme of finite type over a quasi-excellent threefold has a regular char(X)-alteration with snc boundary, and morphisms admit log smooth char(S)-altered desingularization. The new ingredient is tame distillation: after enlarging, an alteration splits as a tame Galois covering over a char(X)-alteration. It rests on the tameness theorem, that p-closed valued fields are tame, which Temkin deduces from Pank's theorem by decompletion in height one and induction on height. It is globalized with Riemann–Zariski spaces and the openness of tame loci. The desingularization then follows Gabber's proof with Sylow subgroups replaced by distillation. Routing: the valued-field ramification theory becomes a new Part II of Tau Ceti Local fields and ramification. Riemann–Zariski spaces, tame distillation and the desingularization theorems join the pending PrimeToDegreeAlterations Part II of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons (Dittmann–Pop, Jannsen). The log structure of a divisor and log regularity are sources for CR.5:log-algebra. Verified fix (2026-09-30, Codex codex-rtOQ9t): general scheme suppliers are consolidated at SF.4; existing henselisation, tame-inertia, Riemann–Zariski and library inputs are reused. The inventory has 79 items (8 library, 3 planned, 68 missing), four routes, thirteen prerequisite entries and ten source findings. Projectivity/exact-boundary and separable-distillation gaps E5–E6 remain explicit blueprint proof obligations; the extraction is complete under section 16, not a completed formal proof.

items.name: Valued fields and valuation rings
items.statement: A valued field is a field k with a non-archimedean (Krull) valuation | | : k → {0} ⊔ Γ, written multiplicatively; k° is its valuation ring and k̃ its residue field.

items.name: Primitive element theorem
items.statement: A finite separable field extension L/K is generated by one element: L = K[t]/(f(t)) for a monic irreducible f.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 2.5.2, p. 109

items.name: Valuative criterion of properness
items.statement: A quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism locally of finite type is proper if and only if it satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proofs of Lemma 3.1.3 and §3.1.5, pp. 113–114

items.name: Local structure of étale algebras (Chevalley)
items.statement: If R → S is of finite presentation and étale at a prime Q, then some localization S_f (f ∉ Q) is standard étale over R, i.e. of the form (R[t]/(f(t)))_g with f monic and f′ invertible.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 3.2.10, p. 117 ([Gro67, IV₄, Th. 18.4.6(ii)])
items.note: The paper uses the local form: an essentially étale extension of valuation rings O_y/O_x is a localization of O_x[t]/(f) with f′(a) a unit.

items.name: de Jong's alteration theorem
items.statement: An integral variety X over a field with a closed Z ⊊ X admits an alteration b : X′ → X (proper, dominant, generically finite, X′ integral) with X′ regular and b⁻¹(Z) an snc divisor ([dJ96, Th. 4.1]).
items.note: L5 plans de Jong's Theorems 4.1 and 6.5; the Galois (Th. 7.3) and semistable (Th. 8.2) variants are item dejong-galois-semistable. L5 retains its accepted de Jong proof/application scope. Accepted PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17 and RS-25 also route general scheme alteration inputs to SF.0/SF.4; consolidate these suppliers through SF.4 rather than adding another general proof in this Part II.

items.name: Raynaud–Gruson flattening by blow-up
items.statement: Let X be qcqs, U ⊆ X a quasi-compact open, and Y → X a quasi-separated finite-type morphism whose restriction to U is flat and locally of finite presentation. There is a U-admissible blow-up X′ → X such that the strict transform of Y is flat and of finite presentation over X′ (Stacks 081R). In the paper U is a dense open; finite presentation of Y → X is not required.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proofs of Lemma 3.1.6 and Theorem 3.3.6, pp. 115, 120
items.note: The general qcqs form is missing and is routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4, coalescing with PAPER-BHATT-18/flatten-finite-type-scheme (accepted route 6, Stacks 081R) and the MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles request. L5 uses a finite-type de Jong special case and must import this common supplier; its narrower plan is not a proof of the general form.

items.name: Normalization in finite extensions
items.statement: For X noetherian, universally Japanese and integral, and K/k(X) finite, the normalization Nor_K(X) is finite over X; for a fine enough modification X₁ → X (e.g. a flattening blow-up), Nor_L(X₁) is a modification of Y = Nor_L(X).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.3, p. 119; proof of Theorem 3.3.6, p. 120
items.note: The general noetherian universally Japanese form is missing and belongs to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4. L5 retains the applicable finite-type/excellent special case; AlgebraicCurves Layer 2 supplies its polynomial-curve case. The general Nagata/Japanese hypothesis and finiteness theorem are not supplied by a relative-normalization construction alone.

items.name: Semistable reduction of multipointed curves after a separable alteration
items.statement: Let S be an integral noetherian quasi-excellent normal scheme. For a flat quasi-projective finitely presented S-curve with smooth generic fibre and an étale horizontal marking (a flat finitely presented closed subscheme of relative dimension zero, disjoint from generic singularities), there is a separable alteration S̄ → S and a projective modification X̄ → X ×_S S̄ giving a semistable multipointed S̄-curve. This is the stable-modification input to Steps 1–3 of Exposé X Theorem 3.4 and Temkin Theorem 4.2.1.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Steps 1–3, p. 122
items.note: Missing; route to PrimeToDegreeAlterations. Import Temkin 2010 Theorem 1.5 (existence after a generically étale alteration), Theorem 1.1 (projectivity of stable modification) and Corollary 1.6 (equivariance). L5/de-jong-5-8-curve-fibration-alteration is the existing projective curve-fibration base case over integral excellent schemes, not the non-proper relative-curve theorem. Exposé X Remark 3.4.1(i) explicitly requires Temkin for this extension.

items.name: Chart criterion for log smoothness between snc pairs
items.statement: For X, Y regular with snc divisors Z, T and f : X → Y with T ×_Y X ⊆ Z, (X, Z) → (Y, T) is log smooth iff near each x there are regular parameters t_i at y defining T and z_j at x defining Z with (1) f*(t_i) = ∏_j z_j^{l_ij}; (2) the kernel and the torsion of the cokernel of l : Z^s → Z^r are finite of order invertible in k(y); (3) X₀ → Y₀ ×_{Spec Z[t]} Spec Z[z] is smooth for small neighbourhoods.
items.note: CR.5:log-algebra plans Kato's chart criteria 'with torsion-order invertibility conditions'; this is its regular-snc specialization.

items.name: The log structure of a divisor
items.statement: For Z ⊂ X closed with complement i : U → X, M_X := O_X ∩ i_*O_U^× defines a log structure (X, Z); it need not be fine (cuspidal curve Spec k[x², x³], Z = {x = 0}), but when X is regular and Z snc it is fs and log regular. A morphism f with T ×_Y X ⊆ Z induces (X, Z) → (Y, T).
items.note: Routed to CR.5:log-algebra as a source, beside the log structures it constructs.

items.name: Log regular log schemes (Kato)
items.statement: An fs log scheme is log regular if at every point the local ring modulo the ideal generated by the non-units of the log structure is regular of the complementary dimension ([Kat94]; [Niz06]); (X, Z) with X regular and Z snc is the basic example.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §1.2.7, p. 100; proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Step 10, p. 123
items.note: Kato's toric singularities are not in CR.5's text, which plans the log algebra they need. Routed to CR.5:log-algebra as a source.

items.name: P-numbers, P-groups, P-extensions and P-closed fields
items.statement: For a set of primes P (complement P′), a P-number has all prime divisors in P, and P(n) is the set of prime divisors of n. A P-group has P-number order; an algebraic extension L/K is a P-extension if [L′ : K] is a P-number for every finite subextension. P-extensions are transitive and closed under subextensions and filtered unions; every K has a maximal P-extension, which is P-closed (no nontrivial P-extensions); a finite extension of a P-closed field need not be P-closed.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II with the field theory it opens with.

items.name: Split towers and separable distillation
items.statement: A tower L/K/k is split if L = l ⊗_k K for some l/k (l linearly disjoint from K with lK = L). An algebraic extension l/k has a separable distillation l/l_i/k (l_i/k purely inseparable, l/l_i separable) iff l = l_s ⊗_k l_i; every finite l/k has a finite extension l′/k with a separable distillation (separable distillation theorem).
items.note: Keep missing. Mathlib IntermediateField.LinearDisjoint and IntermediateField.linearDisjoint_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isSeparable provide linear disjointness of separable and purely inseparable subextensions (the injectivity input). Existence of separable distillations and the full splitting statement remain Part II work.

items.name: Henselian valued fields
items.statement: A valued field k is henselian if k° is a henselian local ring; equivalently, the valuation of k extends uniquely to every finite extension l/k.
items.note: Mathlib has HenselianLocalRing but not the unique-extension characterization for Krull valuations. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Ramification theory of henselian valued fields
items.statement: For k henselian with residual characteristic exponent p: the maximal unramified extension k^u, with (k^u)° the strict henselization and Gal(k^u/k) = Gal(k̃^s/k̃); l/k is totally ramified iff it is linearly disjoint from k^u iff l̃/k̃ is purely inseparable; every algebraic l/k splits uniquely as l/m/k with m/k unramified and l/m totally ramified, and l/k is tame when l/m is a p′-extension, for a finite tame extension [l : k] = [l̃ : k̃]·#(|l^×|/|k^×|), where # denotes the order of the quotient of value groups.
items.note: Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2–4 are the local-field special cases. Import the strictly henselian arbitrary-rank pro-p/tame theorem from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles and profinite Sylow theory from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-2-profinite-sylow-theory. Import the local-ring (strict) henselisation interface from ModularCurves 4D; the Part II develops only the valued-field tower and its comparison over k^u. The displayed degree formula is for finite tame extensions and value groups, not multiplicative groups.

items.name: Tame closure and wild inertia
items.statement: A henselian k has a unique maximal tame extension k^t; the wild inertia W_k = Gal(k^s/k^t) is pro-p, the unique Sylow pro-p subgroup of the inertia group I_k = Gal(k^s/k^u); k^t/k^u is Galois with Gal(k^t/k^u) = Hom(|(k^t)^×|/|k^×|, µ_{k^u}), and |(k^t)^×| is the p′-divisible envelope of |k^×|.
items.note: The Part II imports the strictly henselian arbitrary-rank pro-p Sylow/tame-quotient statement from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles and obtains §2.2.6 by passage to k^u. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group is the local-field special case and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-2-profinite-sylow-theory supplies abstract profinite Sylow theory. Neither of these imported results is planned again.

items.name: Purely wild extensions
items.statement: For k henselian, an algebraic l/k is purely wild if it is linearly disjoint from k^t; equivalently l/k is a totally ramified p-extension; equivalently l̃/k̃ is purely inseparable and |l^×|/|k^×| is a p-group.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Henselization and the basic ramification tower
items.statement: The henselization k^h has ring of integers the henselization of k°; k^u := (k^h)^u, k^t := (k^h)^t give the tower k^s/k^t/k^u/k^h/k, and the subgroup of Gal(k^s/k) fixing k^h is the decomposition group. An algebraic l/k is tame (unramified) if l^h/k^h is; strictly unramified if moreover l̃ = k̃ (k^h/k is the maximal one); henselian if the valuation extends uniquely; totally ramified (purely wild) if linearly disjoint from k^u (k^t).
items.note: Import strict henselisation of local rings from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#4d-regularity-of-a-moduli-problem. Non-strict semilocal henselisation and compatibility with filtered colimits (EGA IV 18.6.8, 18.6.14) are explicit supplier requests to that owner, not claimed already planned by its strict-only text; consolidate with the draft PerfectoidSpaces:P3 henselisation-of-pairs work and the H1/SF.2 request. The Part II constructs only the valuation-ring comparisons and the valued-field tower.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2
items.statement: For a valued field k and finite l/k with l₁, …, l_n the non-isomorphic valued extensions of k on l, l ⊗_k k^h = ∏_i l_i^h.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.3, Lemma 2.3.2 and proof, pp. 104–105
items.note: Semilocal integral closure (Bourbaki) and henselization of semilocal rings (EGA IV 18.6.8). Routed to the valued-fields Part II. Import strict henselisation of local rings from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#4d-regularity-of-a-moduli-problem. Non-strict semilocal henselisation and compatibility with filtered colimits (EGA IV 18.6.8, 18.6.14) are explicit supplier requests to that owner, not claimed already planned by its strict-only text; consolidate with the draft PerfectoidSpaces:P3 henselisation-of-pairs work and the H1/SF.2 request. The Part II constructs only the valuation-ring comparisons and the valued-field tower.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.4 (Prüfer)
items.statement: If l/k is finite and A ⊆ l is an integrally closed k°-subalgebra, every localization of A is a valuation ring.
items.note: Mathlib has no Prüfer domains. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.8 (unramified versus étale)
items.statement: For a finite extension l/k of valued fields: l/k unramified (strictly unramified) ⟺ l°/k° essentially étale (strictly essentially étale) ⟸ l°/k° étale (strictly étale); all three are equivalent when the height of k is finite.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.3.7, Lemma 2.3.8 and proof, pp. 105–106
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Tame and separably tame fields
items.statement: A valued field k is tame if k^a = k^t (every algebraic extension is tame) and separably tame if k^s = k^t; tame fields are perfect since purely inseparable extensions are purely wild.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.11 (henselian extensions)
items.statement: An algebraic extension l/k is henselian iff l and k^h are linearly disjoint over k, and then l ⊗_k k^h = l^h.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II. Import strict henselisation of local rings from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#4d-regularity-of-a-moduli-problem. Non-strict semilocal henselisation and compatibility with filtered colimits (EGA IV 18.6.8, 18.6.14) are explicit supplier requests to that owner, not claimed already planned by its strict-only text; consolidate with the draft PerfectoidSpaces:P3 henselisation-of-pairs work and the H1/SF.2 request. The Part II constructs only the valuation-ring comparisons and the valued-field tower.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.2 (the six properties)
items.statement: For R one of strictly unramified, unramified, tame, henselian, totally ramified, purely wild: (i) in a tower m/l/k, m/k is R iff m/l and l/k are; (ii) filtered unions of R-extensions are R; (iii) for any set of these properties, every valued field has a (non-canonical) maximal extension with them.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.4.4 (splitting k^t/k^u/k^h/k)
items.statement: For a maximal henselian unramified k_hu/k and a maximal tame totally ramified k_rt/k: k^h ⊗_k k_hu = k^u and k^u ⊗_k k_rt = k^t.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: §2.4.6 and Remark 2.4.7 (five equivalent splitting statements)
items.statement: For a class V of valued fields closed under algebraic extensions, with k_w a maximal purely wild extension, the following are equivalent: (0) k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a for some k_w; (1) for every k_w; (2) k_w is tame; (3) k ∈ V is tame iff k = k_w; (4) Gal(k^s/k) → Gal(k^t/k) has a section. They are also equivalent to their separable analogues with a maximal separable purely wild k_sw.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.4.6 and Remark 2.4.7, pp. 108
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.9 (Pank)
items.statement: If k is henselian and k_w is a maximal purely wild extension, then k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a.
items.note: Cited input: Kuhlmann–Pank–Roquette prove (4) by a profinite Schur–Zassenhaus argument and pro-p-freeness of Sylow subgroups; Ershov proves (3) by controlling defect. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Krasner's lemma and continuity of roots
items.statement: Over a henselian valued field, a monic polynomial g of the same degree whose root is close enough to a root of a separable monic f generates the same extension ([End72, 16.8]); roots of monic polynomials depend continuously on the coefficients ([Bri06, Th. 2]).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Lemma 2.5.2, p. 109
items.note: Mathlib's IsKrasner covers complete normed fields, not henselian Krull-valued fields. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.5.2 (decompletion)
items.statement: If k has height one, every tower L/k^h/k with L/k^h separable splits: there is a henselian extension l/k with L = l^h = l ⊗_k k^h.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.5.1, Lemma 2.5.2 and proof, p. 109
items.note: k is dense in k^h (k̂ is henselian); Krasner for finite L, Zorn in general. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.3
items.statement: For k of height one and algebraic l/k: l/k is a maximal separable purely wild extension iff l/k is henselian and l^h/k^h is a maximal separable purely wild extension.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Theorem 2.5.5 (Pank's theorem in height one)
items.statement: If k is a valued field of height one and k_w/k a maximal purely wild extension, then k^t ⊗_k k_w = k^a.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.5.4, Theorem 2.5.5 and proof, p. 110
items.note: Perfect case via k^h and Corollary 2.5.3; general case via the perfection and the equivalence (0) ⟺ (1). Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.6
items.statement: Any p-closed valued field of height one is tame.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Composed valuations and the chain of a finite-height valuation
items.statement: A valuation ring R̃ of k̃ pulls back to a valuation ring R of k composed of (k, k°) and (k̃, R̃); conversely each prime n ⊂ k° exhibits k° as composed of k°_n and k°/n. For k of height d, k_i = (k, k°_i) with k°_i the localization of height i and k̃_i its residue field; the residual characteristic exponents p_i are 1 for i < n and p for i ≥ n (some n).
items.note: Keep missing. Mathlib ValuationSubring.ofPrime and idealOfLE, with idealOfLE_ofPrime and ofPrime_idealOfLE, already identify prime localizations with overrings. The pullback of a residue-field valuation ring and the finite-height chain k_i, k̃_i remain Part II constructions.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.3(i)
items.statement: For l/k algebraic of height d < ∞ and 0 ≤ i ≤ d: l/k is unramified iff both l_i/k_i and l̃_i/k̃_i are unramified.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.2, Lemma 2.6.3(i) and proof, p. 111
items.note: The 'if' direction is [Tem10, Prop. 2.2.2]. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Lemma 2.6.3(ii)
items.statement: l/k is tame iff l_i/k_i and l̃_i/k̃_i are tame and |l_i^×|/|k_i^×| has no nontrivial p-torsion (p = exp.char(k̃)); the last condition can be omitted when p_i = p.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.2, Lemma 2.6.3(ii) and proof, pp. 111–112
items.note: The last step of the printed proof writes 'p = char(K̃_i) divides [L̃_i : K̃_i]'; when p_i = 1 the field K̃_i has characteristic 0, and the prime that matters is the residue characteristic p of K̃_i's own valuation (sourceIssues E4). The conclusion holds. Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Corollary 2.6.4
items.statement: A valued field k of height d < ∞ is tame iff k_i and k̃_i are tame and |k_i^×| is p-divisible; the divisibility condition can be omitted when p_i = p.
items.note: Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: Finite transcendence degree gives finite height
items.statement: A valued field of finite transcendence degree over its prime subfield has finite height (Abhyankar's inequality).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), proof of Theorem 2.6.6, p. 112
items.note: The general Abhyankar inequality is owned once by LocalFieldsPartIIGeneralValuedFields: for a valued extension K/K₀, trdeg(k̃/k̃₀) + dim_Q((Γ/Γ₀) ⊗ Q) ≤ trdeg(K/K₀); rank(v) ≤ rational rank(v), and the restricted prime-field valuation has finite rank. Its finite-transcendence-degree consequence is the stated item. PAPER-SCHOLZE-17/503 also routes the general input to DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8; C8 should import it from this Part II and retain its separate complete-algebraically-closed/modified-topological-transcendence comparison. This import alone does not close that stronger analytic comparison gap.

items.name: Theorem 2.6.6 (tameness theorem)
items.statement: Let k be a valued field of residual characteristic exponent p. If k is p-closed, then k is tame.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §2.6.5, Theorem 2.6.6 and proof, p. 112
items.note: Finite height by induction on d with Corollaries 2.5.6 and 2.6.4; in general, descend a finite l/k to a finitely generated k′ ⊆ k, replaced by its algebraic closure in k, which stays p-closed. The proof cites a nonexistent Corollary 2.5.6(ii) (sourceIssues E3). Routed to the valued-fields Part II.

items.name: de Jong: Galois alterations and altered semistable reduction
items.statement: The alteration of dJ96 Th. 4.1 can be chosen G-Galois (X′/G → X generically radicial, G = Aut_X(X′)) [dJ96, Th. 7.3]; and an integral scheme over an excellent curve admits altered semistable reduction [dJ96, Th. 8.2].
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Gabber's ℓ′-altered desingularization
items.statement: If ℓ is a prime invertible on X, the altered desingularization and altered semistable reduction theorems hold with alterations of degree prime to ℓ ([IT14b, Ths. 2.1 and 2.4]); more generally ℓ′-altered desingularization of finite-type morphisms [IT14b, Th. 3.5], via relative curves [IT14b, Th. 3.4]; in characteristic 0 an actual desingularization of morphisms [IT14b, Th. 3.9].
items.note: The theorem PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and PAPER-JANNSEN-16 route to this Part II; Temkin's Theorems 4.2.1 and 4.3.1 generalize it from P = {ℓ}′ to any P ⊇ char.

items.name: char(X), P-alterations and maximally dominating morphisms
items.statement: char(X) is the set of primes p = char k(x), x ∈ X. For a set of primes P, a P-alteration is an alteration whose degree is a P-number. For noetherian S with generic points η_i, η_S = ⊔ η_i; X → S is maximally dominating if it maps η_X to η_S, equivalently X ×_S η_S is dense in X; an alteration is a proper, surjective, maximally dominating, generically finite morphism.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Resolution of qe threefolds and surfaces
items.statement: Every noetherian quasi-excellent scheme S of dimension at most three is universally resolvable in the embedded sense used in §4.3.2: for every alteration Y → S and nowhere dense closed subset Z ⊂ Y, there is a modification Y′ → Y with Y′ regular and the inverse image of Z the support of an snc divisor. This is the Cossart–Piltant/Lipman input as invoked by Temkin; projectivity of this embedded modification is a separate supplier check required for E5.
items.note: Route resolution in these named proved settings to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4 under accepted RS-25. Cite Cossart–Piltant, J. Algebra 529 (2019), 268–535, doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2019.02.017 (arXiv:1412.0868v2); it was unpublished when Temkin wrote. The blueprint must locate the exact embedded/universal theorem and verify projectivity before using the stronger E5 contract. Build the Lipman surface case compatibly on tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-4-blowups-and-intersection-theory-on-arithmetic-surfaces (normal proper models of curves over a DVR). No claim of a completed general resolution proof is made.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.5 (char(X)-altered desingularization)
items.statement: Let X be a scheme with a nowhere dense closed subset Z, admitting a finite-type morphism to a qe scheme S with dim S ≤ 3. Then there is a projective char(X)-alteration b : X′ → X with X′ regular and b⁻¹(Z) an snc divisor; if S = Spec k with k perfect, b can be chosen separable.
items.note: Proof route: shrink S so that char(S) = char(X), then use the embedded universal-resolution input and Theorem 4.3.1(i),(iii). Projectivity requires the projective form of universal P-resolvability (E5) through 4.3.1(i). It does not follow from the statement of 4.3.1(ii), which controls only b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′). The blueprint must establish from the construction behind (ii) that b⁻¹(Z) itself is snc. The separability claim also needs the separable distillation repair E6. These are explicit proof obligations, not assertions that the printed argument already proves them.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.9 (char(S)-altered desingularization of morphisms)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be maximally dominating of finite type, Z ⊂ X nowhere dense closed, X separated and S of finite type over a noetherian qe threefold. (i) There are char(S)-alterations a : S′ → S, b : X′ → X with regular sources, projective, a quasi-projective f′ : X′ → S′ compatible with f and snc divisors W′ ⊂ S′, Z′ ⊂ X′ with Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′) and (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth. (ii) If S = Spec k with k perfect, moreover a is an isomorphism and b is separable.
items.note: From Theorem 4.3.1(ii),(iii). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. The proof must implement the projective universal-resolvability and exact-boundary repair E5; separability conclusions require E6, with Theorem 4.2.1 used under char(S) ⊆ P as in E1.

items.name: Riemann–Zariski spaces of pointed schemes
items.statement: A pointed scheme is ε : Spec K → X with X quasi-compact and quasi-separated; a modification is a morphism with j an isomorphism and f proper. RZ_K(X) := lim X_i over all modifications, as a locally ringed space, with |RZ_K(X)| = lim |X_i| and O = colim π_i⁻¹O_{X_i}; constructible subsets are preimages of constructible subsets of some X_i. Tight modifications (ε schematically dominant) are cofinal.
items.note: Import the affine dominant-point Huber limit theorem from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian (the zariski-riemann-space-as-limit input, also consumed at DiamondEtaleCohomology:C5). For X = Spec A and a dominant K-point, identify Temkin's construction with that limit using the same Spv carrier. The supplier edge is H1:henselian → PrimeToDegreeAlterations, not the reverse. Tau Ceti already defines ValuationSpectrum with continuous_comap and a SpectralSpace instance, and proves compactSpace_patchTopology; Mathlib proves compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology. Only the pointed-scheme generalization, comparison and missing adapters remain.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.3
items.statement: For X = RZ_K(X): (i) X is compact in the constructible topology and quasi-compact in the Zariski topology; (ii) each stalk O_{X,x} is a valuation ring and x ↦ O_{X,x} is a bijection RZ_K(X) → Val_K(X), the set of morphisms Spec O → X from valuation rings O of K extending the point.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.1.2, Lemma 3.1.3 and proof, p. 113
items.note: [Tem10, Cors. 3.2.4–3.2.5]. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. Import the affine dominant-point Huber limit theorem from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian (the zariski-riemann-space-as-limit input, also consumed at DiamondEtaleCohomology:C5). For X = Spec A and a dominant K-point, identify Temkin's construction with that limit using the same Spv carrier. The supplier edge is H1:henselian → PrimeToDegreeAlterations, not the reverse. Tau Ceti already defines ValuationSpectrum with continuous_comap and a SpectralSpace instance, and proves compactSpace_patchTopology; Mathlib proves compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology. Only the pointed-scheme generalization, comparison and missing adapters remain.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.6 (functoriality and openness)
items.statement: A morphism of pointed schemes (η_L → Y) → (η_K → X) induces ψ : Val_L(Y) → Val_K(X) by restriction, compatible with RZ_L(Y) → RZ_K(X); if Y → X is of finite type, ψ is open and continuous in the Zariski and constructible topologies.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.1.5, Lemma 3.1.6 and proof, pp. 113–115
items.note: Reduce to K = k(X_i) and f flat of finite presentation by flattening; flatness lifts valuations. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Absolute Riemann–Zariski spaces
items.statement: Val_K = Val_K(Spec Z) is the set of all valuation rings of K; Val_K(X)′ ⊆ Val_K, the valuations with a centre on X, is compact in the constructible topology; for any L/K, ψ_{L/K} : Val_L → Val_K is continuous and open.
items.note: Keep missing: TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum, continuous_comap, its SpectralSpace instance and compactSpace_patchTopology, together with Mathlib compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology, supply the carrier/topology. Remaining are the explicit field identification Spv K ≃ {valuation rings of K}, compactness of the centre-admitting image Val_K(X)′ and openness of restriction. E8 corrects the claimed converse to separatedness; only separated X ⇒ injectivity is used.

items.name: Tame, wild and unramified loci; S-, X- and P-tameness
items.statement: For algebraic L/K: L/K is x-tame for x ∈ Val_L if tame for x and ψ_{L/K}(x); Val^t_{L/K} is the tame locus, Val^w_{L/K} its complement; L/K is absolutely tame if Val^t = Val_L, S-tame if S ⊆ Val^t, X-tame if Val_L(X)′-tame (invariant under modification). char(S) is the set of nonzero residue characteristics of S; L/K is P-tame if char(Val^w_{L/K}) ∩ P = ∅; analogously the unramified locus Val^u_{L/K}.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6
items.statement: Any P-closed field K is P-tame; every algebraic extension of it, even when not P-closed, is P-tame too.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6, p. 116
items.note: From the tameness theorem 2.6.6. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.8
items.statement: (i) For L/l/k: Val^t_{L/k} = Val^t_{L/l} ∩ ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^t_{l/k}), and likewise for Val^u. (ii) If L = Kl for subextensions l/k and K/k, then ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^t_{l/k}) ⊆ Val^t_{L/K} and ψ_{L/l}⁻¹(Val^u_{l/k}) ⊆ Val^u_{L/K}.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.10 (openness of the loci)
items.statement: For a finite extension L/K, the tame locus and the unramified locus are open in Val_L.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.9, Lemma 3.2.10 and proof, p. 117
items.note: Unramified: Chevalley's standard étale form is an open condition. Tame: pass to unramified extensions where L′ = K′(x_i^{1/n_i}). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. Implement the minimal-polynomial correction E7 before claiming the étale algebra embeds in L. E9 corrects the internal reference to the first part of this lemma.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.12 (tame distillation for fields)
items.statement: Let L/K be finite, S ⊆ Val_L compact in the constructible topology, and P = char(S ∩ Val^w_{L/K}) its wild primes set. Then there are a finite L′/L and a tower L′/K′/K with K′/K a P-extension and L′/K′ S′-tame, S′ = ψ_{L′/L}⁻¹(S). For any maximal P-extension K̄/K one can take K′ ⊆ K̄ and L′ = LK′.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.2.11, Theorem 3.2.12 and proof, pp. 117–118
items.note: LK̄/K̄ is S̄-tame since K̄ is P-closed; tameness is achieved over finite K_x locally, and quasi-compactness of S̄ with Lemma 3.2.10 makes finitely many suffice. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. E6 adds a separately stated separable variant for separable input, using a maximal separable P-extension; the unrestricted printed theorem is retained.

items.name: Galois alterations, tame actions and tame Galois coverings
items.statement: An alteration f : Y → X is Galois if Y/G → X is generically radicial for G = Aut_X(Y) (k(Y)/k(X) = purely inseparable then Galois with Aut_X(Y) the full Galois group), separable if generically étale. A finite group action is tame if every inertia group G_x (elements fixing x and acting trivially on k(x)) has order invertible in k(x). A Galois covering is a finite separable Galois alteration, tame if Aut_X(Y) acts tamely; Nor_K(X) is the normalization of X in K.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.4
items.statement: If X is noetherian, universally Japanese and integral and L/k(X) is an X-tame Galois extension, there is a modification X′ → X such that Nor_L(X′) → X′ is a tame Galois covering.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.3, Lemma 3.3.4 and proof, p. 119
items.note: The non-tame loci T_i = ∪_{(H,p), p | |H|} Y_i^H ∩ Y_i(p) are closed; a point of RZ_L(Y) in all of them would contradict y-tameness. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.7 (Galois closure preserves tameness)
items.statement: For L/K finite separable with Galois closure L′/K, T ⊆ Val_K, S = ψ_{L/K}⁻¹(T) and S′ = ψ_{L′/K}⁻¹(T): L/K is S-tame iff L′/K is S′-tame.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3, Lemma 3.3.7 and proof, p. 120
items.note: The proof as printed has its directions swapped and primes dropped (sourceIssues E2). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.6 (tame distillation of alterations)
items.statement: Let X be noetherian, universally Japanese and integral, Y → X an alteration, and P = P^w_{Y/X}, the wild primes set of Val_{k(Y)}(X)′ over k(X) (a subset of char(X) bounded by deg f). Then there is an alteration Y′ → Y such that Y′ → X factors as a tame Galois covering Y′ → X′ followed by a P-alteration X′ → X.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §3.3.5, Theorem 3.3.6 and proof, p. 120
items.note: Flatten so that Y = Nor_L(X); apply Theorem 3.2.12; pass to the Galois closure (Lemma 3.3.7); apply Lemma 3.3.4 over Nor_{K′}(X). Lemma 3.3.7 needs L′/K′ separable, which follows because X-tameness includes the trivial valuation. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. E6 adds a separately stated separable variant for separable input, using a maximal separable P-extension; the unrestricted printed theorem is retained.

items.name: Universal P-resolvability and pseudo-projective morphisms
items.statement: A noetherian X is universally P-resolvable if for every alteration Y → X and nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ Y there is a projective P-alteration f : Y′ → Y with Y′ regular and f⁻¹(Z) snc (universally separably P-resolvable if f can be chosen separable). A finite-type morphism is pseudo-projective if it is a local isomorphism followed by a projective morphism ([IT14b, 3.1.6]); for separated morphisms this is quasi-projectivity.
items.note: Projective form required by source issue E5, following Illusie–Temkin Exposé X §3.3.3. Temkin §4.1.4 as printed omits projectivity. The blueprint must prove this stronger form through the construction, including snc of the inverse image itself, rather than infer it from an snc enlargement. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Gabber's modification theorem and monoidal desingularization
items.statement: If a finite group G acts tamely on a log regular (X, T) over a log regular (S, W) with trivial action on (S, W) and inertia specializing, there is a modification (X′, T′) of (X, T)/G with (X′, T′) → (S, W) log smooth ([IT14b, Th. 3.1.5; Th. 1.1]); the monoidal desingularization functor F^log ([IT14a, 3.4.9]) makes the source regular with snc boundary.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §1.3.5, p. 102; proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Step 10, p. 123
items.note: Cited inputs; the PrimeToDegreeAlterations briefs already name Gabber's log-modification proof as supplier work.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 (resolution of relative curves)
items.statement: Let S be noetherian qe with generic points η, f : X → S maximally dominating of finite type, Z ⊂ X nowhere dense closed. Assume S is universally (separably) P-resolvable for a set of primes P with char(X) ⊆ P, X_η is a smooth curve over η and Z_η étale over η. Then there are a projective (separable) P-alteration a : S′ → S, a projective modification b : X′ → (X ×_S S′)^pr and divisors W′ ⊂ S′, Z′ ⊂ X′ with S′, X′ regular, W′, Z′ snc, f′ : X′ → S′ pseudo-projective, (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth and Z′ = c⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′).
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4.2, Theorem 4.2.1 and proof, pp. 121–123
items.note: The [IT14b, Th. 3.4] proof with Step 4 replaced by tame distillation (Theorem 3.3.6). Under the printed hypothesis char(X) ⊆ P, that step needs the repair recorded in sourceIssues E1. The theorem is used only with char(S) ⊆ P. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. Recommend the proved-use scope char(S) ⊆ P (E1): Exposé X §3.3.3 assumes the prime ℓ invertible on S. The separable alternative needs the separate variants of 3.2.12 and 3.3.6 (E6). Use the projective universal-resolvability convention E5, and the log-geometry corrections E10.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(i)
items.statement: Let f : X → S be a maximally dominating finite-type morphism of noetherian qe schemes, and S universally P-resolvable with char(S) ⊆ P. Then X is universally P-resolvable.
items.locator: Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4.3, Theorem 4.3.1(i) and proof, p. 123
items.note: Copies the proof of [IT14b, Th. 3.5] with ℓ′ replaced by P and Theorem 4.2.1 in Step 6 (Step 4 uses an infinite P-extension of a finite field, possible since char(k) ∈ P). Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. The proof must implement the projective universal-resolvability and exact-boundary repair E5; separability conclusions require E6, with Theorem 4.2.1 used under char(S) ⊆ P as in E1.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(ii)
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses and a nowhere dense closed Z ⊂ X, there are projective P-alterations a : S′ → S and b : X′ → X with regular sources, a pseudo-projective f′ : X′ → S′ compatible with f and snc divisors W′, Z′ with Z′ = b⁻¹(Z) ∪ f′⁻¹(W′) and (X′, Z′) → (S′, W′) log smooth.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. The proof must implement the projective universal-resolvability and exact-boundary repair E5; separability conclusions require E6, with Theorem 4.2.1 used under char(S) ⊆ P as in E1.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1(iii)
items.statement: If S = Spec k with k perfect, one can moreover take a an isomorphism and b separable; in particular X is universally separably P-resolvable.
items.note: Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II. The proof must implement the projective universal-resolvability and exact-boundary repair E5; separability conclusions require E6, with Theorem 4.2.1 used under char(S) ⊆ P as in E1.

items.name: Remark 4.3.4 (refinement of Theorem 1.2.9)
items.statement: In Theorem 1.2.9 one can require X′ to be a char(X)-alteration of a subscheme of X ×_S S′ (rather than a char(S)-alteration), by resolving over an open S₀ with char(S₀) = char(X) and then embedding into a char(S)-alteration of S (outline).
items.note: An outline in the paper. Routed to the prime-to-degree alterations Part II.

items.name: Separably P-closed fields are separably P-tame
items.statement: If K has no nontrivial finite separable P-extension, then for every valuation on K whose residual characteristic belongs to P, every finite separable extension of K is tame at every prolongation.
items.locator: Repair E6 of Theorem 4.2.1 Step 4; Lemma 3.2.5 and Theorem 2.5.5
proofSteps: The perfection K^perf is P-closed: finite separable extensions descend after a Frobenius twist, and a perfect field has no nontrivial purely inseparable extensions.
Apply Lemma 3.2.5 to K^perf. Purely inseparable base change identifies absolute Galois, inertia and wild-inertia groups; equivalently (K^perf)^t = K^t K^perf and K^t K^perf ∩ K^s = K^t.
Descend tameness for separable extensions to K. This does not say that all algebraic extensions of an imperfect separably P-closed field are tame.

items.name: Separable tame distillation for fields
items.statement: Let L/K be finite separable, S ⊆ Val_L constructibly compact, and P = char(S ∩ Val^w_{L/K}). There is a finite separable P-extension K′/K inside any chosen maximal separable P-extension of K such that L′ = LK′ is S′-tame over K′, where S′ is the full inverse image of S. In particular L′/K is separable.
items.locator: Repair E6; separable variant of Theorem 3.2.12, p. 118
proofSteps: Use separably-p-closed-tame in a maximal separable P-extension. Since L/K is separable, its compositum stays separable.
Repeat the openness, finite-descent and compactness argument of 3.2.12, taking the finitely many K_x and their compositum inside the maximal separable P-extension.

items.name: Separable tame distillation of alterations
items.statement: For a noetherian universally Japanese integral scheme X and a separable alteration Y → X, put P = P^w_{Y/X}. There is a separable alteration Y′ → Y such that Y′ → X factors through a tame Galois covering Y′ → X′ and a separable P-alteration X′ → X.
items.locator: Repair E6; separable variant of Theorem 3.3.6, p. 120; Theorem 4.2.1 Step 4
proofSteps: Apply the separable field-distillation variant to k(Y)/k(X) and the same compact valuation set.

Use the normalization/modification and Galois-closure argument of 3.3.6; all generic field extensions stay separable. Projectivity required in 4.2.1 must still be tracked through its projective modification/refinement steps.

items.name: Quasi-excellent noetherian scheme
items.statement: A noetherian scheme is quasi-excellent if its affine coordinate rings are G-rings and J-2: their local-ring completion maps have geometrically regular fibres, and every finite-type algebra has open regular locus. Universal catenarity is the extra condition for excellence, not part of quasi-excellence.
items.note: General scheme input of SF.4; no predicate found at the pins.

comparisons: Affine restriction and invariance under scheme isomorphism; separate excellence from quasi-excellence.
consumers: Expose the exact qe hypothesis for resolution and stable modification.

tests: A spectrum of a field satisfies the definition.
A finite-type scheme over a field is quasi-excellent.
Do not infer universal catenarity from the definition alone.

items.name: Universally Japanese and Nagata schemes
items.statement: A scheme is universally Japanese if it is covered by spectra of rings A for which every finite-type A-algebra that is a domain has finite integral closure in every finite extension of its fraction field. In the noetherian setting this is the Nagata condition. Retain noetherianity in the normalization statements used here.
items.note: SF.4 owns the general notion and normalization theorem. AlgebraicCurves Layer 2 supplies the polynomial-curve special case, not arbitrary Nagata schemes.

constructors: Affine cover of universally Japanese rings.
comparisons: Locality and the noetherian Nagata equivalence.
consumers: Finiteness of normalization in finite fraction-field extensions.

tests: A field and a polynomial algebra over a field satisfy the condition.
The curve case agrees with the AlgebraicCurves interface.
Normality alone must not discharge the Japanese hypothesis.

items.name: Regular scheme
items.statement: A locally noetherian scheme X is regular if every local ring O_{X,x} is a regular local ring. At ring level this means that the minimal number of generators of the maximal ideal equals the Krull dimension.
items.locator: Regularity in the conclusions of §§1 and 4; ModularCurves Layer 4D
items.note: Import the scheme predicate from ModularCurves 4D using the existing ring predicates; do not reconstruct regular local rings.

comparisons: Affine regular-ring comparison and isomorphism invariance.
consumers: Regular sources in alteration and boundary contracts.

tests: Spec of a field is regular.
Affine space over a field is regular.
A nonreduced double point is not regular.

items.name: Strict normal crossings support on a regular scheme
items.statement: On a regular noetherian scheme X, an snc support is the support of a reduced effective Cartier divisor locally cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters. The empty support is allowed. A closed subset described as snc means the support of such a divisor, following Exposé X §3.3.3.
items.locator: Every resolution conclusion; Exposé X §3.3.3, p. 159; Stacks 0CBN
items.note: Extend the existing simple-normal-crossings boundary interface of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7a to the regular noetherian setting through CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra; retain one boundary carrier.

constructors: Regular-parameter local equations and the empty boundary.
comparisons: Compatibility with R09.7a on its existing scope and with the divisorial log structure.
consumers: Boundary support in projective universal resolvability.

tests: The coordinate axes in affine two-space have snc support.
The origin alone in affine two-space is not a divisor.
A repeated parameter gives the same support but is not a reduced defining divisor.

items.name: Finite-group quotient glued from invariant affine opens
items.statement: Let a finite group G act on a scheme Y and suppose every orbit is contained in a G-invariant affine open. Glue the affine quotients Spec(A^G) to form Y/G, with its quotient map and categorical universal property. Distinguish the decomposition stabilizer at y from its inertia subgroup, the kernel of the action on k(y). The action is tame when every inertia-group order is invertible in its residue field.
items.locator: §3.3.1–3.3.3 and Theorem 4.2.1 Step 10; SGA 1, Exposé V §1
items.note: Import the affine invariant-ring quotient from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0c-finite-quotients-and-torsors. The non-free gluing and inertia interface are the missing Part II extension; finite-type hypotheses must be checked before asserting that the quotient map is finite.

constructors: Invariant affine quotients and descent on their overlaps.
comparisons: Affine restriction, equivariance and quotient universal property.
consumers: Tame Galois coverings and the Gabber modification quotient.

tests: The trivial group gives Y itself.
On an invariant affine, the quotient is Spec(A^G).
A non-free action is permitted; it is not automatically a torsor.

items.name: Logarithmic Abhyankar lemma
items.statement: Let S be regular noetherian with snc support W. For a finite normal tame Galois covering S̄ → S that is étale over S minus W, the divisorial log morphism (S̄, W̄) → (S, W), W̄ the inverse-image support, is Kummer étale and (S̄, W̄) is log regular. Retain the tameness/invertibility conditions on the inertia orders.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2.1 Step 10, p. 123; Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208 / SGA 1 Exposé XIII §5
items.note: General log input of CR.5:log-algebra. LPV.5 and AlgebraicCurves Layer 8 are the codimension-one/function-field special cases; compare with them rather than duplicate them.

items.name: Log smooth over log regular is log regular
items.statement: For a log-smooth morphism of fine saturated log schemes in the locally noetherian setting, a log-regular target implies a log-regular source. This is a property of the source, distinct from calling the morphism log smooth.
items.locator: Kato, Toric singularities (1994), Theorem 8.2; Theorem 4.2.1 Step 10
items.note: Route to CR.5:log-algebra; the existing chart definitions alone do not supply this theorem.

items.name: Log smoothness of semistable multipointed curves
items.statement: Let S be regular noetherian with snc boundary W, and let (C,D) be a semistable multipointed S-curve, with D étale and disjoint from the relative singular locus, smooth away from W. Equip S with the divisorial log structure of W and C with that of D ∪ f⁻¹(W). In this boundary setting the induced morphism is log smooth, with the usual nodal charts.
items.locator: Theorem 4.2.1 Steps 3 and 10; Exposé X §3.2 and proof of Theorem 3.4
items.note: The relative-curve application belongs to PrimeToDegreeAlterations and imports CR.5:log-algebra charts. The boundary contains the non-smooth fibres; a nodal curve over a trivially logged field is not asserted log smooth with only its marking as boundary.

items.name: A local subring is dominated by a valuation ring
items.statement: For a field K and a local subring A of K there is a valuation subring B of K dominating A; the order is the local-domination order, not just inclusion of rings.

items.name: Flat locally finitely presented morphisms are open
items.statement: A flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation is an open map (indeed universally open).

items.name: Chevalley constructibility
items.statement: If f : X → Y is a quasi-compact, locally finitely presented scheme morphism, Y is qcqs, and T ⊆ X is constructible, then f(T) is constructible.

items.name: Constructible compactness of qcqs schemes
items.statement: A quasi-compact, quasi-separated, quasi-sober prespectral space is compact in its constructible topology. In particular this applies to every qcqs scheme.

prerequisites.citation: L. Illusie and M. Temkin, Exposé X: Gabber's modification theorem (log smooth case), in Travaux de Gabber sur l'uniformisation locale et la cohomologie étale des schémas quasi-excellents, Astérisque 363–364 (2014), 167–212
prerequisites.why: Theorems 2.1, 2.4, 3.1.5, 3.4, 3.5: Gabber's ℓ′-alterations and the proofs Theorems 4.2.1 and 4.3.1 copy.

prerequisites.citation: L. Illusie and M. Temkin, Exposé VIII: Gabber's modification theorem (absolute case), Astérisque 363–364 (2014), 103–160
A. J. de Jong, Smoothness, semi-stability and alterations, Publ. Math. IHÉS 83 (1996), 51–93
F.-V. Kuhlmann, M. Pank and P. Roquette, Immediate and purely wild extensions of valued fields, Manuscripta Math. 55 (1986), 39–67
Yu. L. Ershov, Tame and purely wild extensions of valued fields, St. Petersburg Math. J. 19 (2008), 765–773
prerequisites.why: The valuation-theoretic proof of Pank's theorem.

routes.title: Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes, Part II: prime-to-degree alterations
routes.brief:
This is the PrimeToDegreeAlterations Part II proposed by PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 and PAPER-JANNSEN-16 under the same id; their Gabber ℓ′-alteration briefs remain binding. Prove Temkin's Theorem 1.2.5: for X of finite type over a quasi-excellent scheme of dimension at most three and nowhere dense Z ⊂ X, obtain a projective char(X)-alteration b : X′ → X with X′ regular and b⁻¹(Z) the support of an snc divisor; over a perfect field retain separability. Prove the morphism form 1.2.9 and the universal forms 4.3.1(i)–(iii), with their stated hypotheses, degree restrictions and exact boundary formula, plus Remark 4.3.4.
Cover char(X), P-alterations and maximal domination; Riemann–Zariski spaces of pointed qcqs schemes and Val_K(X), including non-dominant points (3.1.3, 3.1.6); absolute RZ spaces; tame, wild and unramified loci and P-tameness (3.2.5, 3.2.8, 3.2.10); field and alteration tame distillation (3.2.12, 3.3.6); Galois alterations, tame actions and coverings (3.3.4, 3.3.7); the non-free finite-group quotient glued from invariant affine opens, reusing ModularCurves 0C affine quotients. Add the separable variants for separable input in E6, using the separably P-closed/P-tame input from the general-valued-fields Part II. Retain generic separability through normalization, Galois closure and projective refinements.
Universal P-resolvability uses a projective P-alteration of every alteration and its nowhere dense closed subset, with the inverse image itself snc, as in Exposé X §3.3.3 (E5). For 4.3.1(i), prove this exact inverse-image property from the construction behind (ii); an snc enlargement alone does not imply it. Check the embedded/projective Cossart–Piltant input in its supplier before using this strengthened convention. Prove 4.2.1 in the needed scope char(S) ⊆ P (E1), which is Exposé X's base hypothesis and suffices for 4.3.1; a generalization to the printed char(X) hypothesis needs its own descent proof. The separable alternative requires E6. Preserve the E7 minimal-polynomial repair and E8/E10 source corrections.
Import general flattening (Stacks 081R), universally Japanese normalization, quasi-excellence/Nagata definitions, and Cossart–Piltant/Lipman resolution in named proved settings from Scheme and stack foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4); its Lipman input builds on StableReduction Layer 4. Import the accepted de Jong scope from Adic coefficients and comparison with schemes (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5), including its de-jong-5-8-curve-fibration-alteration base case. Extend to non-proper semistable multipointed curves via Temkin 2010 Theorems 1.1 and 1.5 and Corollary 1.6, and prove their boundary log-smoothness. Keep de Jong's Galois/semistable variants, Gabber's ℓ′ theorem, modification theorem and monoidal desingularization in their source-scoped forms.
Import log structures, Kato's chart criterion, log regularity, the log Abhyankar lemma and Kato's log-smooth/log-regular theorem from CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra. Reuse AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7a's boundary carrier and its CR.5 extension to regular noetherian schemes; import regular schemes from ModularCurves 4D on the existing regular-ring predicates. Import tame ramification from LocalFieldsPartIIGeneralValuedFields. Reuse the built TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum, its spectral/patch topology and continuous comap, and Mathlib constructible compactness. Import ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian's affine dominant-point Huber limit theorem, also used by DiamondEtaleCohomology:C5; identify RZ_K(Spec A) with it on the same Spv carrier. The dependency runs H1:henselian → this Part II, never back to H1.
Acceptance: P = {ℓ}′ recovers the source theorem when ℓ is invertible on S; a char(X)-alteration in characteristic zero has degree one because char(X) is empty; distinguish the inverse image of a closed point from an snc enlargement; reject wild inertia as tame; test the separable distillation variant only for separable input. These proof/API obligations belong to the blueprint; no completed Lean proof is claimed here.

routes.title: Local fields and ramification, Part II: ramification theory of general valued fields
routes.brief:
Extend Tau Ceti's Local fields and ramification roadmap from local fields to arbitrary Krull valuations. The final theorem is Temkin 2.6.6: a valued field of residual characteristic exponent p with no nontrivial p-extension is tame. Cover P-extensions and P-closed fields; split towers and separable distillation; henselian valued fields and their valued-field henselization; the decomposition l ⊗ k^h = ∏ l_i^h (2.3.2), Prüfer subalgebras (2.3.4); the ramification tower k^s/k^t/k^u/k^h/k; unramified, strictly unramified, tame, henselian, totally ramified and purely wild extensions (2.3.8, 2.3.11, 2.4.2, 2.4.4); tame and separably tame fields; reformulations 2.4.6; Pank's theorem, Krasner's lemma, height-one decompletion (2.5.2), 2.5.5 and 2.5.6; composed valuations and finite-height chains (2.6.3, 2.6.4); and the general tameness theorem. Add separably P-closed implies separably P-tame for the separable alteration-distillation repair E6, proving invariance of the separable tame tower under perfection.
Import the strictly henselian arbitrary-rank pro-p Sylow/tame-quotient theorem from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles and deduce Temkin §2.2.6 over k^u. Import the local-field cases through LocalFieldsRamification Layers 2–4, explicitly including tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-4-the-tame-quotient-of-the-absolute-galois-group; use tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-2-profinite-sylow-theory for group theory. The supplier edge is H1:valuation-nearby-cycles → this Part II. Import local-ring strict henselisation from tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#4d-regularity-of-a-moduli-problem. Send the additional non-strict semilocal henselisation and filtered-colimit compatibility (EGA IV 18.6.8, 18.6.14) as one supplier request there; its strict-only text does not already establish them. Consolidate draft PerfectoidSpaces:P3 and H1/SF.2 requests with that owner. This Part II proves that the resulting local rings are valuation rings and builds the valued-field tower, without reconstructing the local-ring functors.
Reuse Mathlib's Valuation, ValuationRing, HenselianLocalRing and IsKrasner; ValuationSubring.ofPrime/idealOfLE and their inverse laws for coarsenings; IntermediateField linear disjointness of separable and purely inseparable subextensions. The residue-valuation pullback, finite-height chains and existence of separable distillations remain new work. Own the general Abhyankar inequality, trdeg(k̃/k̃₀) + dim_Q((Γ/Γ₀) ⊗ Q) ≤ trdeg(K/K₀), and rank ≤ rational rank, once here, citing Bourbaki VI §10.3 Corollary 1. DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8 imports it by a Part II → C8 edge and retains its stronger comparison with modified topological transcendence degree; that analytic gap is not closed by the algebraic inequality alone.
Acceptance: discrete local-field notions agree with Layers 2–4; retain field-extension finiteness in [l:k] = [l̃:k̃]·#(|l^×|/|k^×|) for finite tame extensions; an Artin–Schreier extension such as a root of u^p−u=t⁻¹ over F_p((t)) is purely wild; distinguish imperfect separably P-closed from P-closed; use 2.6.4 for a p-closed field of height two. No duplicate Sylow theorem or local-ring henselisation is a Part II output.

sourceIssues.printed: The source assumes universal P-resolvability of S for primes P satisfying char(X) ⊆ P. In Step 4 it invokes Theorem 3.3.6 to enlarge a so that its factorization consists of S̄ → S′, a tame Galois covering, followed by a : S′ → S, a P-alteration.
sourceIssues.correction: Either assume char(S) ⊆ P, which is how Theorem 4.3.1 uses the theorem, or keep char(X) ⊆ P and run Step 4 over S₀ := S minus the fibres over char(S) ∖ char(X) (finitely many, as in §4.3.2), which contains f(X) and has char(S₀) = char(X). Apply Theorem 3.3.6 to S̄ ×_S S₀ → S₀, obtaining a P-alteration and a Galois covering that is tame over S₀. Extend to S by normalization and closure of the modification, and resolve with the P-resolvability of S. Tameness is needed only over f(X), since X̄ lies over S₀ and Step 10 uses tameness of the action on X̄.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem 3.3.6 yields a P^w_{S̄/S}-alteration, where P^w_{S̄/S} is the wild primes set of S̄ → S, a subset of char(S). With only char(X) ⊆ P it may contain primes outside P, at which S̄ → S can be wildly ramified although X is empty there. Then 'a P-alteration' does not follow as written. The paper's main results apply the theorem only through Theorem 4.3.1, where char(S) ⊆ P.
